official.deadline_note: The ER.GO study grant call for a.y. 2026/27 ran 23/06/2026-24/08/2026 at 16:00; the portfolio has no single deadline - Unibo ISEE-based/no-tax-area exemptions run to 30/10/2026 18:00 (late window to 16/11/2026 18:00 with a EUR 100 penalty), 150-hour collaboration applications to 26/11/2026 15:00, ER.GO extraordinary contributions 01/10/2026-01/12/2026, formative vouchers 15/09/2026-10/12/2026, disability contributions 20/01/2027-08/03/2027
official.application_cycle: 2026/2027 academic year; ER.GO publishes a new call for applications each year, indicatively from mid-June
official.status_note: The ER.GO study grant call for a.y. 2026/27 closed on 24 August 2026 at 16:00 (next call expected around mid-June for 2027/28), but other portfolio windows remain open: Unibo ISEE-based exemptions to 30 October 2026, 150-hour collaboration applications to 26 November 2026, ER.GO extraordinary contributions 1 October-1 December 2026
official.tuition_coverage_note: ER.GO study grant recipients are entitled to 'esonero totale dal pagamento delle tasse universitarie' (total exemption from tuition fees) and 'rimborso della tassa regionale' (refund of the regional tax); the merit-based exemption for first-year second cycle students leaves only EUR 157.04 payable (regional tax EUR 140, EUR 16 stamp duty, EUR 1.04 insurance)
benefits: Esonero totale dal pagamento delle tasse universitarie e rimborso della tassa regionale: total exemption from tuition fees and refund of the regional tax for ER.GO study grant recipients

Borsa di studio ER.GO: a sum of money to support the expenses of your studies, diversified by the economic condition of the family unit (ISEE bracket) and by student status - in sede, pendolare or fuori sede
Total merit-based exemption for students enrolled in the first year of second cycle degree programmes: only EUR 157.04 payable
'150 hours' collaboration study grant: EUR 8.50 for each hour worked, up to a maximum of EUR 1,275 tax-free, with 1,371 positions for a.y. 2026/27
ER.GO international mobility contribution of up to EUR 600 per month for scholarship-eligible students on international mobility programmes, additional to Erasmus+ and MUR contributions
Accommodation in university halls of residence in the Region, grants covering part of the cost of rent, discounted canteen meals and public transport passes at special prices
eligibility: Enrolled or enrolling on a first, second or single cycle degree programme at the University of Bologna
Economic requirement: ISEE, or the documentation required by the call for families with income and/or assets only outside Italy, below the thresholds established in the call
Merit requirement: a minimum number of credits (CFU) for each academic year, per the merit tables
Enrolment requirement: enrolment finalised at the university within the deadlines set out in the competition announcement

For the merit-based exemption: first cycle degree obtained at the University of Bologna in a.y. 2025/26 by 31 July 2026 (30 November 2026 for healthcare professional degree programmes), within the course's established duration, with a mark of no less than 110/110

Scheme-specific statuses: international protection for the MUR-CRUI and Ministry of the Interior refugee schemes; citizenship in a listed particularly poor/developing or non-OECD country with family income and assets only abroad for the reduced fixed fee
requirements: Application must be submitted every academic year, even without prior enrolment, by the mandatory and non-extendable call deadlines

Declaration of economic situation (ISEE or documentation on foreign income and assets) submitted via the ER.GO portal; applications made at a CAF or with university credentials must be finalised with PEC or PIN by the same deadline
A minimum number of credits (CFU) acquired each academic year to access the benefits and confirm their assignment
Domicile documentation for fuori sede status: self-certification by 03/11/2026 16:00, documentation by 14/01/2027

For the 150-hour collaboration: application on Studenti Online no later than 26 November 2026 at 15:00, completion of the compulsory online health and safety training, and a certificate of Italian language knowledge at level A2 for non-Italian citizens
documents: ISEE affidavit or, for students whose family has income and/or assets only outside Italy, the documentation on foreign income and assets required by ER.GO
Domicile self-certification and supporting documentation for students claiming fuori sede status
Certification of civil disability percentage of 66% or more under Law 104/92, for disability-related fee exemptions
First cycle degree certificate showing the final mark, for the total merit-based exemption

Certificate of Italian language knowledge at level A2, for the 150-hour collaboration (not required if you hold an Italian upper secondary diploma, a degree from a course taught in Italian, or have already demonstrated A2 Italian)
selection_criteria: ER.GO study grant: amounts and ranking are differentiated by the economic condition of the family unit (ISEE bracket) and by student status - in sede, pendolare or fuori sede

150-hour collaboration, in order of priority: eligibility status when not awarded an ER.GO study grant; ECTS credits acquired from 10 August 2025 to 10 August 2026; ISEE value, priority to the lowest; age, priority to the youngest
Merit-based exemption: first cycle degree obtained on time, within the course's established duration, with a mark of no less than 110/110
Unibo for Refugees study awards: credits obtained and grades achieved
Merit data are exchanged directly between the university secretariats and ER.GO near the deadlines
coverage: Total exemption from tuition fees and refund of the regional tax for ER.GO scholarship recipients
A cash study grant to support the expenses of the academic path, differentiated by ISEE bracket and student status
Accommodation in the university halls of residence in the Region and grants covering part of the cost of rent
Discounted meals at university canteens and participating establishments; public transport passes at special prices in Bologna, Cesena, Forli, Ravenna and Rimini
International mobility contribution of up to EUR 600 per month, additional to Erasmus+ and MUR contributions, revocable if the sum of other mobility contributions exceeds the monthly threshold
application_method: ER.GO benefits: apply online on the ER.GO portal (servizionline.er-go.it/domande2), at a CAF or with university credentials, finalising the application with PEC or PIN by the same deadline
University of Bologna calls (150 hours, study awards, special-reserve procedures): apply on Studenti Online (studenti.unibo.it), selecting 'Calls'
Live calls are published on the University's official notice board at bandi.unibo.it
The reduced fixed fee (Flat Tax) is requested on the ER.GO portal form, declaring that the family's income and assets are only outside Italy and accepting the flat-rate fee
official.application_route: Apply once per academic year: ER.GO benefits through the ER.GO online portal (CAF or university credentials, finalised with PEC or PIN), University of Bologna calls through Studenti Online
official.citizenship_residency: Most ER.GO benefits require enrolment at a university of the Emilia-Romagna region rather than Italian citizenship; the reduced fixed fee requires citizenship in a listed particularly poor or developing country, or a non-EU non-OECD country, with family income and assets only abroad; refugee schemes require international protection status; specific reserved places target students from the Palestinian Territories and asylum seekers, refugees or displaced persons and Iranian female students
official.international_eligibility: Yes - international students have dedicated ER.GO guidance including a 'Focus on: Scholarship' page and a guide to the application announcement, are eligible for ER.GO study grants on the same economic, merit and enrolment terms, and can access the reduced fixed fee; the portfolio also signposts MAECI scholarships for international students and MUR-CRUI scholarships for holders of international protection
official.subject_or_agency_requirement: Most benefits are open to students of any degree programme; ER.GO merit tables and call provisions differ by campus and course (including STEM course lists), and the Unibo for Refugees study awards require holding an ER.GO, UNICORE or CRUI scholarship in a.y. 2025/26
official.duration: One academic year; the application must be submitted every academic year, even without prior enrolment
official.description: The University of Bologna presents this as financial support 'at every stage of your studies', with opportunities 'tailored to your needs': needs- and merit-based tuition fee reductions and exemptions, ER.GO study grants, accommodation, canteen and transport concessions, collaboration and mobility grants, and dedicated routes for international students, refugees and students from conflict-affected countries.
official.region: Italy - University of Bologna campuses (Bologna, Cesena, Forli, Ravenna, Rimini, Ozzano dell'Emilia, Imola); ER.GO benefits are administered by the Regional Authority for the Right to Higher Education of Emilia-Romagna
official.program_type: University study grants and fee subsidy portfolio

verification.notes: Checked the Unibo study grants hub plus merit exemption, reduced fixed fee, 150-hour and refugees pages, and ER.GO borsa di studio, mobility, deadlines, amounts and call pages on unibo.it and er-go.it; per-scheme amounts (EUR 1,275 150-hour maximum, EUR 600/month mobility, EUR 2,500 study awards, EUR 4,608 EPOS, EUR 500-1,400 Flat Tax, EUR 157.04 first instalment) are confirmed from official pages, but the portfolio publishes no single portfolio-wide funding figure and no travel or English-language requirement

applicant_utility.summary: The biggest money in this portfolio runs through one door: the annual ER.GO call, which pairs an ISEE-based cash grant with total tuition-fee exemption and a refund of the EUR 140 regional tax, but only if you also hit the annual credit minimums. That call opens around mid-June and the a.y. 2026/27 window has already closed (24 August 2026, 16:00), so the realistic next shot is the call expected around mid-June 2027 for a.y. 2027/28. If your family's income and assets are all outside Italy, decide deliberately between the ISEE-based route and the reduced Flat Tax (EUR 500-1,400 plus EUR 157.04 for a.y. 2026/27) before applying, because the two are incompatible. Meanwhile the portfolio keeps paying out of season: the 150-hour collaboration grant (up to EUR 1,275, apply on Studenti Online by 26 November 2026), Unibo's ISEE exemption window (to 30 October 2026) and ER.GO extraordinary contributions (1 October-1 December 2026) are all live now.
applicant_utility.best_fit: Students already enrolled or about to enrol at Unibo with genuine financial need or top first-cycle marks, including international students with family income abroad and holders of international protection, who have dedicated routes
application_readiness_checklist: Sort yourself into a specific scheme first: this entry bundles dozens of separate calls and each has its own route, criteria and window, so applying to the wrong one is the most common wasted effort

Have your ISEE ready before the ER.GO call opens in June, or, if your family has income and assets only abroad, prepare ER.GO's foreign income and asset documentation instead - this is the usual bottleneck
Check that your enrolment is correctly recorded in your Student Administration Office: ER.GO suspends your ranking position until the Secretariat confirms your career is active
If you will claim fuori sede (non-resident) status, file the domicile self-certification by 3 November 2026 at 16:00 and keep the supporting documents, because your grant tier depends on this status

For the 150-hour grant, apply on Studenti Online before 26 November 2026 at 15:00, complete the compulsory safety training, and non-Italian citizens must hold an A2 Italian certificate before starting work
Download and read the current ER.GO call PDF in full: ER.GO warns the contents change year to year and that the deadlines are mandatory and non-extendable
common_rejection_risks: Missing the ER.GO call deadline - the a.y. 2026/27 window closed on 24 August 2026 at 16:00 and ER.GO states its deadlines are mandatory and cannot be postponed
Failing to finalise enrolment by the deadline: ER.GO states that missing the enrolment deadline means losing eligibility for the benefits
ISEE or foreign-income documentation rejected as incomplete or incorrect - Unibo warns that benefits obtained this way are revoked and the maximum fee charged
Falling short of the annual CFU minimum: the study grant is not non-repayable funding and its assignment is confirmed only against merit credits each year
Being suspended in the provisional ranking because your student career is not yet active at your Secretariat - eligibility in the provisional list does not mean the grant is assigned
applicant_utility.estimated_uncovered_costs: Even under total exemption you always pay the EUR 157.04 first instalment (EUR 140 regional tax, EUR 16 stamp duty, EUR 1.04 insurance); Flat Tax students pay EUR 500-1,400 plus that amount unless ER.GO-eligible; beyond that you still fund books, personal travel home and any cost above the residence and canteen benefits
document_audit: ISEE must match the right household and reference year; students with foreign income or assets must supply ER.GO's specific documentation, which is checked thoroughly

Domicile evidence drives your grant tier (in sede, pendolare, fuori sede): the self-certification window closes 3 November 2026 at 16:00 while full documentation runs to 14 January 2027 - do not mix them up

The merit-based exemption depends on the exact degree date and mark: Unibo first-cycle degree obtained in a.y. 2025/26, by 31 July 2026 (30 November 2026 for healthcare professional programmes), within course duration, no less than 110/110
Dual citizens must state where family income and assets sit: Flat Tax only stands if they are exclusively in a particularly poor or non-OECD country
For the 150-hour collaboration, certificates for every completed safety module must reach the assigned facility before work starts
alerts: The flagship ER.GO scholarship window for a.y. 2026/27 closed on 24 August 2026 at 16:00; ER.GO publishes each new call indicatively from mid-June, so diarise June rather than September
The reduced fixed fee (Flat Tax) and the ISEE-based No Tax Area exemption are incompatible - accepting Flat Tax is a formal choice on the ER.GO form and forfeits the ISEE route
Unibo's ISEE-based / no-tax-area benefit runs to 30 October 2026 at 18:00, with a late window to 16 November 2026 that carries a EUR 100 late-payment fee
Accepting the ER.GO international mobility contribution recalculates a commuter or non-resident holder's scholarship down to the in-sede amount - weigh the choice when asked via Dossier Utente
The 150-hour grant pays only after the collaboration ends: provisional rankings appear around late December 2026 and assignments by January 2027
applicant_utility.submission_workflow: One application per academic year: ER.GO benefits via the ER.GO online portal (CAF or university credentials, finalised with PEC or PIN by the same deadline), Unibo calls via Studenti Online, with each benefit then ranked and published separately on ER.GO's ranking pages and bandi.unibo.it
